title: Reconstruct Market Boundaries
coreMove: Look across one accepted market boundary until a different buyer, alternative, complement, emotion, or trend changes the search field.
sourcePressure: Use the six paths framework to minimize search risk by looking across alternatives, strategic groups, buyer groups, complements, functional-emotional orientation, and time.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Thinking reconstruction means making a wild leap outside the business instead of systematically looking across known borders.

sourceAnchors.name: six paths framework
sourceAnchors.detail: official support names six directions for reconstructing market boundaries and reducing search risk
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The six paths turn market search from wandering into a set of doors: alternatives, groups, buyers, complements, emotion, and time.

sourceAnchors.name: Bloomberg
sourceAnchors.detail: official example support gives a narrow buyer-group shift case
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Bloomberg is useful here as a reminder that a different buyer group can redefine what counts as value.

sourceAnchors.name: Viagra
sourceAnchors.detail: official example support gives a narrow functional-emotional orientation shift case
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Viagra shows how a category can move when the emotional job is treated as part of the value, not an embarrassment outside it.

hook: Do not open with a competitor scoreboard, a war metaphor, or a generic market map.
Do not use A crowded market is not..., The real strategy is..., or What if growth... as reusable shells.
counterintuition: Avoid Most people assume... but actually... and The opposite is true.
Avoid turning every chapter into competition bad, creativity good.
tryThisNow: Avoid Set a timer for 60 seconds and list... as a repeated action.
Avoid generic reflect on your strategy prompts.
examples: Avoid conference-room whiteboard workshops as the default scene.
Avoid repeating mugs, markers, dosing cups, bike helmets, radiators, bus depots, classrooms, narrow kitchens, or generic dashboard scenes.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.audience: an operations lead whose agency misses island first visits after discharge
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether patients receive care or fall through a transport gap
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she tapes the ferry timetable beside discharge notes and sees the agency competing with travel friction, not other agencies
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The ferry timetable hangs crooked beside three hospital discharge folders

exampleSpecs.domain: language lessons competing with rest and bus timing
exampleSpecs.audience: an adult education operator serving exhausted shift supervisors
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether workers choose class, rest, or nothing after long shifts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he must choose whether to redesign around the alternative of going home, not another language school
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You watch the 10:12 p.m. bus leave while Nicolas counts eight empty chairs

exampleSpecs.domain: wedding cookware gifts and the social job of guests
exampleSpecs.audience: a retailer squeezed by online cookware pricing
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether wedding guests choose a safer gift outside the cookware category
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she shifts from selling pans to solving the guest fear of giving something impersonal or duplicate
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Astrid one returned copper pan to notice the real rival was a safe gift card

exampleSpecs.audience: a city planner trying to raise first-time bike-share use
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether nervous riders see the service as freedom or public embarrassment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a commuter admits the helmet station is not the problem; being watched while wobbling is
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "I know where the bikes are," the commuter tells Diego, "I just do not want everyone watching me start."
mustAvoid: bike shop commuter example from chapter 1

exampleSpecs.domain: restaurant supply delivery and receiving friction
exampleSpecs.audience: a wholesaler focused on product quality while delivery friction grows
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether chefs keep buying when morning receiving wrecks prep
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she traces churn to the complementary receiving process around the product, not to tomato quality
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 5:58 a.m., Kasia watches parsley crates block the pastry bench

exampleSpecs.audience: a nonprofit director watching attendance change
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether programs fit the next wave of older adults and family caregivers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he predicts crafts will recover, then voicemail patterns reveal caregiving schedules as the trend to design across
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Voicemails stack up with the same clipped apology: cannot come before noon

skillTargets: identify which market boundary is being crossed
choose a systematic six-path search move
avoid direct-rival benchmarking when an alternative or complement matters more

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one boundary around your offer and label it: alternative, buyer group, complement, emotion, or time.
